3. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 341 of 1982 in the court of the then learned Munsif, Shariatpur, impleading the respondents as defendants praying for declaration of title to the suit land and confirmation of possession there-in and if found out of possession, then recovery of Khas possession in the suit land alleging, inter alia, that the suit land belonged to one Kurban Ali Matubbar and by successive devolution the suit land devolved upon the plaintiff, who possessed the same but the same was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendants who threatened to disposes the plaintiff and accordingly instituted the suit. 

 10. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and perused the judgment of the Appellate Division and other materials on record. Mr. S. K. Shaha, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that as the plaintiff-respondent already prayed in his plaint that if it is found that the plaintiffs had been dispossessed from the land in suit during pendency of the suit, no amendment petition is necessary for deleting the prayer for confirmation of possession, and on the basis of the said prayer, as made in the plaint, a decree for recovery of khas possession should have been allowed by the Appellate Division. 

 12. We have heard the learned Senior Advocate counsel for the petitioner and pursued the judgment of the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division found that the defendant proved the sale certificate in support of the auction sale and the sale deeds and rent receipts showing acquisition of title and also their possession in the suit land vide the Exhibits D. E F H I J K and L but despite such proof the trial court as well as the High Court Division decreed the suit by finding title and possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff without considering the documentary evidence which has caused miscarriage of justice. The Appellate Division further held that the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 shows that the plaintiffs were dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants during pendency of the suit but despite such dispossession the plaintiffs did not amend the plaint incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession by deleting the original prayer for confirmation of possession but the trial as well as the High Court Division decreed the suit although the plaintiffs were admittedly dispossessed by the defendants during pendency of the suit and no prayer for recovery of possession was made by the plaintiffs. In view of the aforesaid finding of the Appellate Division we do not find any ground for review our judgment.
